# BINDING CONSISTENCY LEDGER — Egyptian Arabic Listening Pod (15 Scenes)

## 1. TRANSLITERATION
جيمس = James
آنا = Anna
مانشستر = Manchester
لندن = London
فرنسا = France
ديفز = Davies
جونز = Jones

(All other names — Sarah, Kareem, Ahmed, Mona, Yasmin, Hana — remain as written; Egyptian speakers recognise these without transliteration.)

## 2. PRICES

| Source | Local Amount (Spoken) |
|--------|----------------------|
| 8 pounds 40 | ثمانية وأربعين جنيه |
| 12 pounds 50 | مية وخمسين جنيه |

*Rationale: Coffee shop total (~48 EGP, realistic for 4–5 drinks + water); taxi ride (~150 EGP, realistic 20–25 min Cairo traffic ride). Amounts stay distinct and monotonic.*

## 3. TARGET-LANGUAGE NAME
**لغة مصري** (spoken as: "اللغة المصرية" or colloquially "اللغة الملصرية" / "الكلام المصري")  
*Pin usage: whenever the script names the language, use "لغة مصري" or "اللغة المصرية" — never MSA "اللغة العربية".*

## 4. RECURRING LINES

| Canonical | Egyptian Arabic Rendering |
|-----------|--------------------------|
| Good morning. What can I get you? | صباح الخير. إيه اللي تأخذه؟ |
| Would you like to sit-in or takeaway? | هتقعد هنا ولا تيك أواي؟ |
| Yes, of course. | تمام، بالتأكيد. |
| Could I pay by card? | أدفع بالكارت؟ |
| Do you have contactless? | عندك كونتاكتلس؟ |
| That's [amount] altogether. | ده [amount] كل حاجة. |
| Excuse me. | لو سمحت / من فضلك. |
| Thank you very much. / Thank you. | شكراً جزيلاً / شكراً. |
| Goodbye. / See you. | مع السلامة / شُفت كل شوية. |
| What can I get you? (general) | إيه اللي تأخذه؟ |
| I'm learning Egyptian Arabic. | أنا بتعلم اللغة المصرية. |
| You speak very good Egyptian Arabic. | أنت بتتكلم لغة مصري تمام التمام. |
| I'm on holiday. | أنا هنا في أجازة. |
| Welcome. | أهلاً بيك / أهلاً وسهلاً. |
| Is everything alright? | كل شي تمام؟ |
| Could I see [item]? | ممكن أشوف [item]؟ |
| Can I have [item]? | أقدر آخذ [item]؟ |
| I'd like [item], please. | عايز / عايزة [item] من فضلك. |

*(All scenes using these formulas render identically. Gender agree: "عايز" for male learner, "عايزة" for female.)*

## 5. REGISTER

| Relationship | Unmarked Polite Register |
|--------------|--------------------------|
| Customer ↔ Staff (barista, bartender, waiter, pharmacist, assistant, receptionist, driver) | **2nd person singular honorific with "من فضلك / لو سمحت"**: treat all service staff as formal-polite (حضرتك avoided as too stiff for café; "أنت" + politeness formulae = right register). |
| Stranger ↔ Stranger (tourist ↔ local, passenger ↔ passenger, guest ↔ receptionist) | **2nd person singular with "من فضلك"**: warm but formal. |
| Friend ↔ Friend (learner ↔ friend in Scene 15) | **2nd person singular, drop "من فضلك"**, use first names. Warm and direct. Occasional "يا" + name. |
| Neighbour ↔ Neighbour (Scene 1, 5) | **2nd person singular, light politeness ("تصبح على خير")**; familiar but respectful. |

*Gender: address male as "إزيك" (masc.), female as "إزيك" (fem. form); "تصبح على خير" (masc.) vs "تصبحي على خير" (fem.).*
